intent: Make a bounded region scroll with the kit's own scrollbar in place of the platform's native one.
typical_uses: A fixed-height or fixed-width panel whose content can outgrow it (a long list, a log, a wide table)

instead.note: No kit component replaces it; wrapping the whole page moves scrolling off the document, so the browser no longer restores the scroll position on history navigation.

dont_use_when.situation: Content that never outgrows its box

instead.note: The scroll machinery measures and positions a scrollbar that never shows.

dont_use_when.situation: A chat transcript that should follow the newest message while the user is at the bottom

invariants.text: Every child, including an extra ScrollBar, is rendered inside the scrolling viewport element, not as a direct child of the root.
ScrollArea always composes one vertical ScrollBar and the corner of its own; a horizontal scrollbar appears only when a consumer adds a ScrollBar with `orientation="horizontal"`.
The built-in vertical ScrollBar is not mounted while the content does not overflow vertically; it takes no `keepMounted` from ScrollArea.

The root sets no height or width of its own (scroll-area.module.css gives `.root` only `position: relative`), so it scrolls only once a size is imposed on it by `style`, `className` or its layout parent.

anti_patterns.dont: Leave the ScrollArea unsized and expect it to scroll
anti_patterns.do_instead: Give it a definite height or width (a fixed size, or a stretched flex or grid cell); a `max-height` alone does not work, because the viewport's `height: 100%` needs a definite height to resolve against

anti_patterns.dont: Add a second vertical ScrollBar as a child
anti_patterns.do_instead: Add only a horizontal one; ScrollArea already renders the vertical bar

overflowEdgeThreshold.states: overflowEdgeThreshold is a pixel threshold, either one number for every edge or an object of per-edge numbers
overflowEdgeThreshold.because: Base UI types it `number | Partial<{ xStart; xEnd; yStart; yEnd }>`, and the compiler emits one JSON type per property. It sets how far the content must be scrolled past an edge before the root's overflow edge attributes apply.

render.states: render replaces the rendered element with one the caller supplies
render.because: Base UI's render prop takes an element or a function of the scroll area's own state, so its type is a union of a React element and a callback - the compiler emits one JSON type per property.

style.states: style accepts a function of the scroll area's state as well as a plain style object
style.because: Base UI widens React's `CSSProperties` to `CSSProperties | ((state) => CSSProperties)` so a caller can style off the primitive's own state (scrolling, hasOverflowX, hasOverflowY, ...). The compiler emits one JSON type per property, so nothing is asserted; the kit's own styling goes through scroll-area.module.css, not through this.

unexposed_parts.reason: The scrolling element; ScrollArea renders it around its children with the kit's viewport class, and the kit exports no component for it.
Rendered once by ScrollArea where the two scrollbars meet; Base UI sizes it from the measured scrollbars and the kit gives it no class.

good.title: Wide content scrolling on both axes

bad.title: Importing the viewport part
bad.why: The kit exports no ScrollAreaViewport; ScrollArea renders the viewport itself around its children.
